subject: Colours in stacked bar plot (categorical data)

messages.author: 79c1df91b327de3b
messages.subject: Colours in stacked bar plot (categorical data)
parts:
ggplot2ers,

I have a variable with a large number of categories (often >50
different taxonomic assignments). I am trying to generate a stacked
bar plot, but the number of categories is often making the colours
bleed together.


>ggplot(subject1.phylum.log_table,aes(LogGroup,Count,fill=Phylum))+geom_bar(position="fill",colour="white")+coord_flip()+theme_bw()

Is there a way to randomize the order of colours to stop similar
colours from being adjacent? Any other suggestions?

Any help/pointers greatly appreciated.

Michael Lynch

Ph.D. Candidate
Department of Biology, University of Waterloo

Waterloo, Ontario, Canada N2L 3G1

messages.subject: Re: Colours in stacked bar plot (categorical data)
parts:
Hi Michael,
You can use scale_fill_manual (see ?scale_manual), and specify the
colors directly. There is also scale_fill_brewer(), but it won't work
with so many levels.

Best,
Ista

messages.author: 859894b0c2171566
messages.subject: Re: Colours in stacked bar plot (categorical data)
parts:
One way around the limit of scale_fill_brewer is to use scale_fill_manual and repeat the Color Brewer colors, e.g:

scale_fill_manual(values=rep(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(12, "Set3"), 5))

With so many colors you're going to end up with similar colors anyways, but at least this way any group of 12 adjacent colors will be distinct.

messages.subject: Re: Colours in stacked bar plot (categorical data)
parts:
Thanks Ista,

I was hoping to avoid the manual fill, but it will work well for these
plots. Paired with the Cleveland plots idea (thanks Dennis) different
taxonomic depths will be easy to deal with. Phylum distribution can be
managed with the more traditional stacked bar plots while order and
genus, with many more categories, will be better suited to Cleveland
plots.

Thanks all.

Michael
